instructions: Read the book again from the page images and this text only. Do not open data/pages/ or data/analyses/ for this work until `recheck score`.

pages.text: Amo loves playing in the mielie garden and listening to the birds sing.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Amo's place and her love of the garden and its birds are set

illustration.only_in_image: A bird swoops at a ripe cob beside Amo: the later culprit is in the picture before the text names it.

pages.text:
Every day after school, she goes to count the mielies.
“Mielies! Mielies!”
She calls out.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Her daily after-school ritual of counting the mielies is introduced

pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: She counts six; the baseline number is fixed

illustration.only_in_image: Six cobs stand in a row so the reader can count along and check the number.

pages.text:
“Come on, Amo! Let’s have lunch!”
Koko calls her.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Koko calls her in for lunch, ending the day's visit

illustration.only_in_image: Koko is shown as an older woman in a headscarf; the text never says who Koko is.

pages.text:
“When can we eat the mielies, Koko?” Amo asks.
“Soon,” Koko always answers.
pages.label: INFERRED
pages.change: Amo's wish to eat the mielies is stated and deferred with 'soon'

pages.text:
The next afternoon Amo goes to count the mielies.
1 … 2 … 3 … 4 … 5 …
Oh no!
pages.label: INFERRED
pages.change: The count stops at five: something is wrong

illustration.only_in_image: A bird's tail at the top of the frame and scattered kernels hint at who took the cob.

pages.label: INFERRED
pages.change: She recounts on her fingers and the count is still five

illustration.only_in_image: Bird feathers and loose kernels surround her counting hand: the thief's trace.

pages.text:
“Koko!
One mielie is missing!”
“Let’s have lunch now, we’ll check the mielies tomorrow.”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Amo names the loss; Koko postpones checking to tomorrow

pages.text:
Amo goes to the garden with Koko the next day.
“Mielies! Mielies!” she calls out.
1 … 2 … 3 … 4 …
She stops.
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Next day, with Koko, the call and count repeat and stop at four

illustration.only_in_image: Brown feathers drift among the cobs: birds have been there.

pages.text:
“Koko! Now two mielies are missing! What happened?”
“Hmm … I think the birds ate them,” says Koko.
Amo is sad.
“Do we have to chase them away?”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Two are gone; Koko suspects the birds; Amo is sad and asks if they must chase them

illustration.only_in_image: A bird perches on a cob and pecks it, confirming Koko's guess.

pages.text:
“I have an idea!” says Koko.
“Let’s get some plastic bottles.”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: Koko has an idea and asks for plastic bottles

pages.text: “See! Now the mielies are safe, and you can still see the birds.”
pages.label: OBSERVED
pages.change: The mielies are protected and the birds can still be watched

illustration.only_in_image: Each cob wears a clear bottle sleeve; how the idea works is shown only in the picture.
